name: Wingu Africa / Djibouti Data Centre (DDC)
developer: Wingu Africa / Djibouti Data Centre SARL
notes: Wingu says its Djibouti Data Centre is the country's primary carrier-neutral digital infrastructure hub with colocation, direct access to AMS-IX Djibouti, and links to major submarine cable systems. DCD reports DDC in Djibouti City opened in 2013 and hosts DjIX.

name: Wingu Africa DJI02 / TO7 Technology Park data center and carrier-neutral CLS
notes: Wingu announced in October 2021 that it partnered with TO7 Network to develop a carrier-neutral data center and cable landing station in Djibouti. TO7 states the new carrier-neutral data center is designed, developed, funded and operated by Wingu, with TO7 owning the cable landing station. Baxtel reports DJI02/TO7 Technology Park was officially inaugurated in November 2024; DataCenterMap lists JIB-1/Djibouti City 2 with 5,000 kW IT load, 2,000 sqm colocation space and 1,000 cabinets.

name: Djibouti Telecom Ras Dika Cable Landing Station colocation center
notes: Djibouti Telecom began construction of a new three-floor cable landing station in Djibouti City in 2021; the third floor was reserved for colocation to host cloud/GAFAM providers closer to African users. Submarine Networks update says the site was named Ras Dika CLS and was fully operational on 2023-08-07.

name: PAIX JIB1 Djibouti data center
developer: PAIX Data Centres and Djibouti Sovereign Fund
notes: PAIX announced a joint venture with the Djibouti Sovereign Fund to construct a 50,000 sq ft cloud- and carrier-neutral data center in Djibouti City. DCD reports JIB1 is planned for 5 MW IT capacity and scheduled to open in 2026; Mobile Europe describes up to 5 MW of critical power with first phase expected in 2026.
